nocturnal

nok-TUR-nul — rhymes with journal · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Something that is nocturnal is active mainly at night rather than during the day.

Owls are nocturnal, hunting while the forest sleeps.

Example

Nocturnal animals like bats and raccoons emerge from their hiding places once the sun sets, moving through the darkness with ease and hunting while other creatures sleep.

Nocturnal describes creatures that are naturally active and adapted to hunting at night by their biology and behavior — not just animals that happen to be awake at night. It's more precise than 'night animal' because it emphasizes their evolved adaptation to darkness and nighttime activity as their natural state.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

nighttime: Nighttime simply says when something happens — during the hours of full darkness, after the sun is down. Nocturnal says what a creature is: built by nature to be active at night. A noise can be a nighttime noise; only a living thing can be nocturnal.

dark: Dark describes the absence of light itself — a dark room, a dark sky — and by extension things linked to night. Nocturnal describes behavior, not lighting: a nocturnal animal is one whose active hours come at night, however bright the moon happens to be.

midnight: Midnight names the deepest part of the night, the middle hours of darkness. Nocturnal covers the whole night shift: a nocturnal animal may hunt from dusk to dawn, not just in the dead middle. Midnight is a point in time; nocturnal is a way of living.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

diurnal: active during the daylight hours instead

daytime: occurring while the sun is up

Where it sits · how fully activity belongs to the night — diurnal → crepuscular → strictly nocturnal → nocturnal

diurnal vs. nocturnal: Diurnal is the exact opposite of nocturnal: a diurnal animal is active during the day, while a nocturnal one wakes and hunts at night.

crepuscular vs. nocturnal: Crepuscular falls between diurnal and nocturnal — a crepuscular animal is active at dawn and dusk, at the edges of darkness, while a nocturnal one is active in the full night itself.

strictly nocturnal vs. nocturnal: Strictly nocturnal is even stronger than nocturnal: a nocturnal animal is mainly active at night, while a strictly nocturnal one is active only at night, with no daytime exceptions at all.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — nocturn-

Root — nocturn-: belonging to the night (Latin nox, noctis, 'night'; the fossilized time-suffix -urnus is folded in) (Latin)

Suffix — -al

Suffix — -al: relating to (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Latin nocturnus, 'belonging to the night,' grows from nox/noct- ('night') plus a time-marking ending; add -al ('relating to') and you get nocturnal — relating to and active during the night rather than the day.

Use the root in a new word: equinox

Use the root in a new word: equinox: Sailors once timed long voyages around each equinox — nox, the Latin 'night,' hides at its end, the same root that makes nocturnal animals creatures of the night.

Word Choice

neutral / formal

Nocturnal is the precise term in biology and nature writing to describe creatures that are naturally active at night. In casual conversation, 'night animal' works fine, but nocturnal is more specific and scientific.
